title: Garder le son : les changements des verbes en -er
summary: Handle nous commençons and mangeons, accent changes, and the appeler/jeter and acheter/geler families.
objectives: Preserve soft c and g before -ons.
Distinguish changing stems from regular endings.
Use accented and doubled-consonant patterns without rejecting accepted spelling variants.

sources.label: OQLF: rectified forms including morcèle and ruissèle, consulted 2026-09-07

sections.title: Only nous needs ç or an extra e in these present forms
paragraphs: The regular -er endings remain unchanged. In -cer verbs such as commencer (begin) and avancer (move forward), write ç before -ons to keep the soft s sound. In -ger verbs such as manger (eat) and partager (share), keep an e before -ons to preserve the soft g sound. The other present endings already begin with e and need no repair.
points: The cedilla goes on c, not on the vowel.

sections.title: Some stems change to è before a silent ending
paragraphs: For many verbs with e or é in the last stem syllable, that vowel becomes è before the silent endings -e, -es and -ent. It stays unchanged with nous and vous. Lever (raise), mener (lead) and peser (weigh) illustrate e → è; préférer (prefer) and répéter (repeat) illustrate é → è. Change the last relevant vowel, not every accent in the word.
points: The person endings are still the regular -er endings.

sections.title: Learn appeler and jeter separately from acheter and geler
paragraphs: Appeler (call) doubles l before a silent ending; jeter (throw) doubles t. Their derivatives such as rappeler (call back/remind) and rejeter (reject) keep that pattern. Acheter (buy) and geler (freeze) instead use è before silent endings. Nous and vous use the unchanged stem in all four verbs.

Traditional spelling gives several other -eler/-eter verbs doubled consonants, for example épeler → j'épelle (spell). The 1990 recommendations permit è for those verbs other than appeler, jeter and their derivatives: j'épèle, je ruissèle. Both established traditional and rectified forms are accepted. Do not apply a claim that all -eler/-eter verbs must double. In this lesson the main production models use the unambiguous appeler, jeter, acheter and geler patterns.
points: Appeler/jeter keep their doubled consonants where required in both spelling systems.

production_task.prompt: Plan a shared meal in three sentences. Say what you prefer, what you buy and what you share, using je and nous.
production_task.model_answer: Je préfère la soupe. J'achète des légumes. Nous partageons le pain.
production_task.translation: I prefer soup. I buy some vegetables. We share the bread.
rubric: Use è in préfère and achète.
Keep regular endings despite the stem spelling changes.
